findings.title: Small-action buttons are no longer right-aligned after switching .small-action to flexbox
findings.body:
.small-action is now a flex container (line 264). Its .small-action-desc child has no flex-grow, so it shrinks to the width of its text instead of spanning the row. The old 4em left padding that made it a full-width block is also gone.

The .small-action button rule (lines 306-310) still uses `float: right`. If the buttons sit inside .small-action-desc, they now float to the right edge of a narrow content-sized box. If they are direct children of .small-action, floats are ignored on flex items. Either way, the delete/edit buttons on small action posts move next to the description text instead of the right edge of the post.

Fix: give .small-action-desc `flex: 1 1 auto` (plus the -webkit-box-flex/-ms-flex equivalents), or use `margin-left: auto` on the buttons instead of the float.

findings.title: Header extra-info flex item can't shrink below its content width; long titles may push the panel out
findings.body:
.extra-info-wrapper is now a flex item of `.d-header .contents`. Its min-width defaults to `auto`, and nothing in this change sets `min-width: 0`, `overflow: hidden` or flex-shrink behaviour on it.

When the docked header shows a long, non-wrapping topic title, the item's minimum width becomes the full title width. It then won't shrink, and the `.panel` with the notification/user icons (order 3, `margin-left: auto`) is pushed past the right edge of the header. Previously the floated layout constrained this.

Fix: add `min-width: 0` (or `overflow: hidden`) and an explicit flex basis/shrink to .extra-info-wrapper.

findings.title: Legacy-prefix mixins pass modern values verbatim to old-spec properties with different semantics
findings.body:
`align-items($alignment)` copies its argument into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties accept `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so any future caller using those values emits invalid declarations for the browsers the prefixes target. `-ms-align-items` is not a real property and is dead output.

`order($val)` has the same problem: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based (default 1, values must be >= 1), while `order` defaults to 0. As a result, `order(0)` or negative values are invalid in the legacy model, and `order(1)` orders elements differently in legacy vs. modern browsers.

The current callers (center, baseline, 2, 3) happen to work. The mixins should map the values, or document that they only accept safe values.

findings.title: Float layout removed, but legacy -webkit-box fallback can't right-align the panel with auto margin
findings.body:
The change removes `.title { float: left }` and `.panel { float: right }` and relies on `margin-left: auto` on .panel to push it to the right.

The flexbox mixin explicitly emits `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` for old-spec-only browsers. The 2009 box model does not support auto margins for main-axis distribution; it uses box-pack or box-flex instead. In those browsers the panel would sit immediately after the title/extra-info instead of at the right edge. Browsers without flexbox at all get a stacked header, since no float fallback remains.

Either drop the legacy box prefixes, or add a legacy-compatible way to push the panel right (for example a flexing spacer, or box-flex on .extra-info-wrapper).
